subject: ela
intro: When you read nonfiction, you learn real facts about the world. Good readers ask questions while they read, then find the answer right in the text. When you answer, point to the exact words that prove it. Ask WHO the text is about, WHAT happens, WHERE and WHEN it happens, WHY things happen, and HOW they work. Referring to the text means you can show the sentence that gives the answer, instead of guessing.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A honeybee visits hundreds of flowers each day. As it drinks the sweet nectar, yellow dust called pollen sticks to its fuzzy body. When the bee flies to the next flower, some of that pollen rubs off. This helps the flower make seeds.

WHAT sticks to the bee's body while it drinks nectar?

steps: The question asks WHAT sticks to the bee.
The passage says, "yellow dust called pollen sticks to its fuzzy body."
That sentence names the answer directly.
solution.answer: Pollen sticks to the bee's body. The passage says, "yellow dust called pollen sticks to its fuzzy body."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Harriet Tubman was born into slavery in Maryland. She escaped to freedom in 1849. After she was free, she went back many times to lead other enslaved people north to safety. People called her Moses because she guided so many to freedom.

WHY did people call Harriet Tubman "Moses"?

steps: The question asks WHY she was called Moses.
The passage says she "guided so many to freedom."
That is the reason for the nickname.
solution.answer: People called her Moses because she guided so many people to freedom, just as Moses did in the Bible story. The passage says, "she guided so many to freedom."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Most desert animals rest during the hot day. The fennec fox sleeps in a cool underground burrow while the sun is high. When the air turns cool at night, the fox comes out to hunt for insects and small animals.

WHEN does the fennec fox come out to hunt?

steps: The question asks WHEN the fox hunts.
The passage says, "When the air turns cool at night, the fox comes out to hunt."
So the fox hunts at night.
solution.answer: The fennec fox comes out to hunt at night. The passage says, "When the air turns cool at night, the fox comes out to hunt."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A volcano is an opening in the Earth's surface. Deep underground, melted rock called magma builds up. When the pressure gets too strong, the magma pushes up and bursts out the top. Once it reaches the air, this melted rock is called lava.

HOW does lava reach the air, according to the passage?

steps: The question asks HOW lava gets out.
The passage says the magma "builds up" until "the pressure gets too strong."
Then it "pushes up and bursts out the top."
solution.answer: The melted rock builds up underground until the pressure gets too strong, then it pushes up and bursts out the top of the volcano. The passage says it "pushes up and bursts out the top."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The Great Wall of China is one of the longest structures ever built by people. Workers built it long ago to keep enemies from crossing into China. Parts of the wall are so wide that soldiers could walk along the top.

WHY did workers build the Great Wall of China?

steps: The question asks WHY the wall was built.
The passage says it was built "to keep enemies from crossing into China."
solution.answer: Workers built it to keep enemies from crossing into China. The passage says they built it "to keep enemies from crossing into China."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A spider is not an insect. Insects have six legs and three body parts. A spider has eight legs and only two body parts. Spiders also spin silk to make webs that trap the insects they eat.

HOW many legs does a spider have?

steps: The question asks HOW many legs a spider has.
The passage says, "A spider has eight legs."
The number comes straight from the text.
solution.answer: A spider has eight legs. The passage says, "A spider has eight legs and only two body parts."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Rain does not fall from just any cloud. First, warm air rises and cools, and tiny drops of water form a cloud. The drops bump into each other and join to make bigger drops. When the drops grow too heavy to float, they fall as rain.

WHY do the water drops finally fall as rain?

steps: The question asks WHY the drops fall.
The passage says the drops "grow too heavy to float."
Being too heavy makes them fall.
solution.answer: The drops fall because they grow too heavy to float. The passage says, "When the drops grow too heavy to float, they fall as rain."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The first airplane flight lasted only twelve seconds. In 1903, two brothers named Orville and Wilbur Wright built a flying machine near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. Orville flew it about the length of a soccer field before it touched back down.

WHERE did the Wright brothers fly their machine?

steps: The question asks WHERE the flight happened.
The passage says it was "near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina."
solution.answer: They flew it near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. The passage says the brothers "built a flying machine near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Sea turtles begin life on a sandy beach. A mother turtle crawls onto the shore at night and buries her eggs in the sand. Weeks later, the baby turtles hatch and dig their way up. Then they hurry to the ocean, where they will spend most of their lives.

WHO buries the eggs in the sand, and WHERE do the baby turtles go after they hatch?

steps: The WHO: the passage says "A mother turtle... buries her eggs in the sand."
The WHERE: after hatching, the babies "hurry to the ocean."
Point to both details in the text.
solution.answer: A mother turtle buries the eggs in the sand. After they hatch, the baby turtles hurry to the ocean. The passage says they "hurry to the ocean, where they will spend most of their lives."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The recycling truck comes to Maple Street every Wednesday. Workers empty the blue bins full of paper, cans, and bottles. These materials are taken to a center where they are cleaned and made into new products, so fewer new materials must be used.

Ask one WHEN question and one WHY question about this passage, then answer each using the text.

steps: A WHEN question: When does the recycling truck come? Answer: every Wednesday.
A WHY question: Why is recycling helpful? Answer: so fewer new materials must be used.
Each answer points to a sentence in the passage.
solution.answer: Sample WHEN: 'When does the truck come?' -> every Wednesday. Sample WHY: 'Why does recycling help?' -> so "fewer new materials must be used." Both answers come straight from the text.
